ei.subject: 영어2
ei.title: Microbes and Health — The Hidden Heroes Inside Us

fullPassage:
A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are clusters of bacteria in different parts of the body, such as on the surface or in the deep layers of the skin, in the mouth and the nose, and in the lungs and the stomach. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, reside in the gut. This may sound somewhat frightening, but these bacteria have a crucial and positive influence on our health. The first scientist who paid attention to these microbes in the gut and their importance was Ilya Mechinikov, who won the Nobel Prize in 1908 for his studies on the immune system. He was living in Paris in the late 19th century when thousands of people were suffering from cholera, a disease that was sweeping the European continent. As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease, which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. Remarkably, he didn't get sick. Intrigued, he decided to increase his sample size and recruited a colleague to do the same. The colleague didn't get sick either. But when he tested on another colleague, the poor man became critically ill and almost died. What made them react to the same disease in different ways? By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented it. After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were essential for human health, and that the right balance of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease. Sadly, this view was not widely accepted at the time and was eventually forgotten after Mechinikov died in 1916.

A decade later, antibiotics were discovered. Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. Moreover, people have come to see all germs as threats to good health, and as a result, they have done their best to keep their bodies clean of them. A war has been waged on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them. Unfortunately, this attitude has had harmful effects on health, resulting in a rise in allergies and immune deficiencies.

Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new light. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes. By occupying our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there. Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning. They also facilitate our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be rejected. Therefore, having insufficient germs or losing important ones leads to various health problems. Some microbes help the stomach digest some vegetables and milk. If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk, which eventually leads to an unbalanced diet and poorer health. Other bacteria help the body produce vitamins B and K, as well as important amino acids. Some microbes in the gut determine whether particular drugs are toxic to the liver and whether or not other drugs will work to combat a heart condition. Other microbes regulate the appetite hormone, which makes a person feel full or hungry. Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat. One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. Similarly, doing the reverse made the lean mouse gain weight.

Some researchers who have realized the crucial role of microbes are trying to apply this knowledge to cure people. Instead of using antibiotics, they have found that introducing or increasing the necessary germs that the person lacks can cure some diseases. For example, there were people who had a terrible form of diarrhea, so they had to go to the bathroom up to 20 times a day. These people had not been helped by antibiotic therapy. Researchers transplanted some of the good microbes from a healthy donor into these patients' guts. One day after they received their transplant, all their symptoms cleared up and the diarrhea vanished. They were essentially healthy again. The bacterial community in their own guts came to resemble the donor's bacterial community. Given this knowledge, nutritionists suggest the following ways to keep our guts healthy. One of the easiest ways to do this is through our food. Good microbes can be found in many of the foods we eat and whatever else gets to our mouths. By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, or choosing a diet packed with good, fresh nutrients, such as garlic, onions, and unprocessed grains rich in fiber, we can cultivate good microbes. Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food. Heavily processed foods such as frozen food, packaged snacks, and canned food not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals that damage the good microbes in our guts. Another way to increase beneficial microbes is to spend more time in nature. Places with diverse life forms, such as woods, beaches, parks, or even small farms and gardens, are abundant with diverse bacteria that germ-free urban environments lack. In addition, we should use antibiotics wisely; we must use them much less frequently. Although antibiotics play a crucial role in keeping us healthy by eliminating dangerous germs, they cannot tell good bacteria from bad ones. Therefore, whenever we use antibiotics, we inevitably damage beneficial bacteria as well as the harmful bacteria that we want to get rid of. If we can affect microbes and they can affect our bodies, it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.

questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] The first scientist who paid attention to these microbes in the gut and their importance was Ilya Mechinikov. [해석] 장 속 미생물에 주목한 최초의 과학자는 일리야 메치니코프였다.
det.correct: who는 주격 관계대명사로, 선행사 the first scientist를 수식한다. 관계절 내에서 paid의 주어 역할을 한다.
wrongs: ① which — 선행사가 사람(scientist)이므로 which 사용 불가 ❌

💡 선행사가 사람 + 관계절 내 주어 역할 → who

Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs.

det.correct: giving은 전치사 by 뒤에 오는 동명사이다. by + V-ing = '~함으로써'의 의미이다.

② given — 과거분사는 전치사 뒤에서 동명사 역할 불가 ❌
④ to give — to부정사는 전치사 by 뒤에 올 수 없다 ❌

questions.stem:
(A), (B)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
... which eventually led him (A)[eat / to eat] food (B)[containing / contained] the cholera bacteria.

det.ref: [원문] which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. [해석] 그것이 결국 그가 콜레라 박테리아가 포함된 음식을 먹도록 이끌었다.
det.correct: (A) lead + 목적어 + to부정사: 'led him to eat'이 올바른 구조. (B) containing은 현재분사로 food를 능동적으로 수식: '포함하고 있는 음식'.
wrongs: ① (A) eat – (B) containing: lead는 to부정사를 취함, 동사원형 불가 ❌
③ (A) eat – (B) contained: 두 가지 모두 틀림 ❌
④ (A) to eat – (B) contained: food는 박테리아를 능동적으로 포함하므로 contained(수동) 부적절 ❌
det.tip:
💡 lead + O + to부정사 = ~가 ...하도록 이끌다
⚠️ 현재분사(containing) vs 과거분사(contained): 주어가 능동이면 -ing, 수동이면 -ed

questions.passage: By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented it. After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were essential for human health, and that the right balance of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease. Sadly, this view was not widely accepted at the time and was eventually forgotten after Mechinikov died in 1916.
questions.stem:
밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.
Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria ⓐsupported and ⓑstimulated the cholera's growth, while other species ⓒpreventing it. Sadly, this view was not ⓓwidely accepted at the time.

det.ref: [원문] while other species prevented it. [해석] 반면 다른 종은 그것을 막았다. 해설: supported, stimulated와 병렬 구조이므로 prevented(과거형)이 되어야 한다. preventing(현재분사)은 병렬 구조를 깨뜨린다.
det.correct:
ⓐ supported — ✅ found that 절의 과거 동사
ⓑ stimulated — ✅ supported와 병렬, and로 연결
ⓒ preventing — ❌ prevented가 올바름 (while절의 동사, 병렬)
ⓓ widely — ✅ 부사, accepted를 수식
det.tip:
💡 while절의 동사도 주절과 같은 시제여야 한다. supported/stimulated와 병렬이면 prevented.
⚠️ 병렬 구조: A supported and stimulated ... while B prevented ...

questions.passage: Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new light. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes. questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 부분의 어법상 올바른 형태를 고르시오.
... they prevent harmful germs from growing there.

det.ref: [원문] they prevent harmful germs from growing there. [해석] 그들은 해로운 세균이 그곳에서 자라는 것을 막는다.
det.correct: prevent A from V-ing = A가 ~하는 것을 막다. 전치사 from 뒤에 동명사 growing이 온다.
wrongs: ① grow — 전치사 from 뒤에 동사원형 불가 ❌
② grown — 과거분사는 전치사 뒤 동명사 역할 불가 ❌
④ to grow — to부정사는 from 뒤에 올 수 없다 ❌
det.tip:
💡 prevent/stop/keep + O + from + V-ing = ~가 ...하는 것을 막다
⚠️ from 뒤에는 반드시 동명사(-ing)

questions.passage: One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. Similarly, doing the reverse made the lean mouse gain weight.
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 부분의 문법적 설명으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
... transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight.

det.ref: [원문] transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. [해석] 마른 쥐의 장 박테리아를 과체중 쥐의 위에 이식하는 것이 과체중 쥐의 체중을 줄게 했다.
det.correct: transplanting은 동명사로, 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 한다. '이식하는 것'이라는 뜻. 동사 made의 주어이다.
wrongs: ① 현재분사 (진행의 의미) — 분사구문이 아니라 주어 역할이므로 현재분사 아님 ❌
② 동명사 (전치사의 목적어) — 전치사 뒤가 아닌 문장의 주어 역할 ❌
④ 현재분사 (명사 수식) — 명사를 수식하는 것이 아니라 문장의 주어 ❌
det.tip:
💡 동명사(V-ing)가 문장 맨 앞에서 주어 역할: Transplanting ... made → '이식하는 것이 ~하게 했다'
⚠️ 동명사 주어 vs. 현재분사 구문: 동사(made)의 주어이면 동명사

questions.passage: Heavily processed foods such as frozen food, packaged snacks, and canned food not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals that damage the good microbes in our guts. Another way to increase beneficial microbes is to spend more time in nature. Places with diverse life forms, such as woods, beaches, parks, or even small farms and gardens, are abundant with diverse bacteria that germ-free urban environments lack.
questions.stem:
밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.
Heavily ⓐprocessed foods not only ⓑlacks beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals ⓒthat damage the good microbes in our guts. Another way to increase beneficial microbes ⓓis to spend more time in nature.

det.ref: [원문] Heavily processed foods ... not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain ... [해석] 심하게 가공된 음식은 유익한 박테리아가 부족할 뿐만 아니라... 해설: 주어 foods는 복수이므로 lacks(3인칭 단수)가 아닌 lack이어야 한다.
det.correct:
ⓐ processed — ✅ 과거분사, foods를 수식 (가공된)
ⓑ lacks — ❌ 주어 foods(복수)이므로 lack이 올바름
ⓒ that — ✅ 관계대명사, chemicals를 수식
ⓓ is — ✅ 주어 Another way(단수)에 일치
det.tip:
💡 주어-동사 수일치: 복수 주어(foods) → 복수 동사(lack). not only A but also B 사이에 끼어있어도 주어를 잘 파악!
⚠️ Another way(단수) → is, Heavily processed foods(복수) → lack

questions.passage: We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth. If we can affect microbes and they can affect our bodies, it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings.
questions.stem:
(A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
We need to start (A)[thinking / to think] of the microbes as a part of our bodies and (B)[take / taking] care of them just as we take care of our skin. It is time to stop (C)[thinking / to think] of microbes and ourselves as different beings.

det.ref: [원문] We need to start thinking of ... and take care of them ... / stop thinking of ... [해석] 우리는 미생물을 몸의 일부로 생각하기 시작하고 돌봐야 한다 / 다른 존재로 생각하는 것을 멈춰야 한다. 해설: (A) start + V-ing/to V 모두 가능하나 원문은 thinking. (B) need to start thinking ... and (need to) take care — 병렬 구조로 take가 적절. (C) stop + V-ing = ~하는 것을 멈추다.
det.correct:
✅ ② (A) thinking – (B) take – (C) thinking
❌ ① (A) thinking – (B) taking – (C) to think
❌ ③ (A) to think – (B) take – (C) thinking
❌ ④ (A) to think – (B) taking – (C) to think
det.tip:
💡 start + V-ing/to V 모두 가능. stop + V-ing = ~하는 것을 멈추다 (stop + to V = ~하기 위해 멈추다). 병렬: need to start ... and (need to) take.
⚠️ stop thinking(생각을 멈추다) ≠ stop to think(생각하려고 멈추다)

det.ref: [원문] it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. [해석] 둘을 따로 이야기하는 것은 거의 의미가 없다.
det.correct:
① inevitably — ✅ '불가피하게', 항생제 사용 시 유익한 박테리아도 불가피하게 손상
② perfect — ❌ 원문은 little(거의 없는). 서로 영향을 주고받으므로 따로 이야기하는 것은 의미가 '거의 없다'는 문맥. perfect(완벽한)는 정반대.
③ different — ✅ '다른', 미생물과 우리 자신을 다른 존재로 보는 것을 멈추자
④ part — ✅ '일부', 미생물을 몸의 일부로 생각하자
wrongs: ① inevitably — 항생제가 좋은 균도 불가피하게 손상시킨다는 맥락에 적절 ✅
③ different — 미생물과 인간을 다른 존재로 생각하는 것을 멈추자는 맥락에 적절 ✅
④ part — 미생물을 몸의 일부로 생각하자는 맥락에 적절 ✅
det.tip:
💡 make little sense = 의미가 거의 없다 ↔ make perfect sense = 완벽히 이치에 맞다
⚠️ 서로 영향을 주고받으므로 '따로 이야기하는 것'은 의미가 없다 → little이 적절

questions.passage: By occupying our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there. ( __________ ), people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning. They also facilitate our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be rejected. ( __________ ), having insufficient germs or losing important ones leads to various health problems.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (가), (나)에 들어갈 연결사로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected ... Therefore, having insufficient germs ... leads to various health problems. [해석] 그러므로 건강한 박테리아 군집을 가진 사람은 영향을 받지 않을 수 있다 / 그러므로 불충분한 세균은 건강 문제를 초래한다.
det.correct:
✅ ③ Therefore — Therefore: 두 빈칸 모두 앞 문장의 인과 관계를 나타내는 결론이므로 Therefore(그러므로)가 적절.
(가) 미생물이 먼저 점유하면 → 그러므로 건강한 사람은 영향 안 받음.
(나) 면역 체계를 촉진함 → 그러므로 세균이 불충분하면 문제 발생.
wrongs: ① However — Moreover: However는 역접, (가)에 역접 관계 없음 ❌
② For example — Nevertheless: For example은 예시인데, 새로운 정보 제시 ❌
④ In contrast — Similarly: In contrast는 대조인데, 인과 관계 ❌
det.tip:
💡 Therefore = 그러므로 (인과 관계의 결론). 원인 → Therefore → 결과
⚠️ However(그러나), Moreover(게다가), In contrast(대조적으로)는 맥락 불일치

questions.passage: Remarkably, he didn't get sick. Intrigued, ⓐ<u>he</u> decided to increase his sample size and recruited a colleague to do the same. The colleague didn't get sick either. But when ⓑ<u>he</u> tested on another colleague, the poor man became critically ill and almost died. What made ⓒ<u>them</u> react to the same disease in different ways? By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented ⓓ<u>it</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ가 가리키는 대상이 나머지 셋과 다른 것은?

det.ref: [원문 해석] ⓐ he = 메치니코프 / ⓑ he = 메치니코프 / ⓒ them = 메치니코프, 첫 번째 동료, 두 번째 동료 (세 사람) / ⓓ it = cholera's growth (콜레라의 성장)
det.correct:
ⓐ he = 메치니코프 (흥미를 느끼고 표본 크기를 늘림)
ⓑ he = 메치니코프 (다른 동료에게 실험)
ⓒ them = 세 사람 (메치니코프 + 동료 2명)
ⓓ it = 콜레라의 성장 → ❌ 나머지는 모두 사람(들)이지만 ⓓ만 콜레라의 성장을 가리킴
det.tip:
💡 prevent it → it = the cholera's growth. 문맥: 일부 박테리아는 콜레라 성장을 촉진, 다른 종은 '그것(성장)'을 막음.
⚠️ them(세 사람)과 it(콜레라 성장)의 지칭 대상 구별

questions.passage: Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. Moreover, people have come to see all germs as threats to good health, and as a result, they have done their best to keep their bodies clean of them. A war has been waged on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them. Unfortunately, this attitude has had harmful effects on health, resulting in a rise in allergies and immune deficiencies.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "A war has been waged on microbes"의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] A war has been waged on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them. [해석] 미생물에 대한 전쟁이 벌어졌고, 사람들은 거의 한 세기 동안 미생물을 죽이려고 했다.
det.correct:
✅ ② 사람들이 모든 미생물을 적극적으로 제거하려 해 왔다. — 항생제 남용과 모든 세균을 위협으로 보는 태도의 비유적 표현.
❌ ① 과학자들이 미생물 연구를 위해 경쟁했다 — 전쟁은 '제거'의 비유이지 '연구 경쟁'이 아님
❌ ③ 미생물 사이에서 생존 경쟁이 벌어졌다 — 미생물 간 경쟁이 아닌 인간 대 미생물의 전쟁
❌ ④ 새로운 항생제를 개발하기 위한 국제 협력이 시작되었다 — 협력이 아닌 미생물 제거 노력
det.tip:
💡 'wage a war on ~' = ~에 대한 전쟁을 벌이다 (비유적 표현: 적극적으로 없애려 함)
⚠️ 문맥: 항생제의 기적적 힘 → 남용 → 모든 세균을 위협으로 봄 → 제거 전쟁

ch: 과학자들이 미생물 연구를 위해 경쟁적으로 노력해 왔다.

questions.passage: Some microbes help the stomach digest some vegetables and milk. If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk, which eventually leads to an unbalanced diet and poorer health. Other bacteria help the body produce vitamins B and K, as well as important amino acids. Some microbes in the gut determine whether particular drugs are toxic to the liver and whether or not other drugs will work to combat a heart condition.
questions.stem: 다음 중 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.ref: [원문 요약] 미생물의 역할: ① 채소와 우유 소화 도움, ② 결핍 시 불균형 식단, ③ 비타민 B·K 생산 도움, ④ 약물의 간 독성 및 심장 치료 효과 판별
det.correct:
✅ ④ '장 속 미생물은 비타민을 분해하여 몸 밖으로 배출하는 데 관여한다' — 원문은 비타민을 '생산(produce)'하는 것이지 '분해·배출'이 아님.
❌ ① 일부 미생물은 위장이 채소와 우유를 소화하도록 돕는다 — 원문 일치 ✅
❌ ② 미생물이 부재하면 불균형한 식단으로 이어질 수 있다 — 원문 일치 ✅
❌ ③ 장 속 미생물은 특정 약이 간에 독성이 있는지 판별한다 — 원문 일치 ✅
det.tip:

⚠️ 선지의 '분해·배출'과 원문의 '생산'은 정반대 방향

questions.passage: The first scientist who paid attention to these microbes in the gut and their importance was Ilya Mechinikov, who won the Nobel Prize in 1908 for his studies on the immune system. He was living in Paris in the late 19th century when thousands of people were suffering from cholera, a disease that was sweeping the European continent. As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease, which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. Remarkably, he didn't get sick.
questions.stem: Mechinikov에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

questions.passage: One of the easiest ways to do this is through our food. Good microbes can be found in many of the foods we eat and whatever else gets to our mouths. By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, or choosing a diet packed with good, fresh nutrients, such as garlic, onions, and unprocessed grains rich in fiber, we can cultivate good microbes. Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food. Heavily processed foods such as frozen food, packaged snacks, and canned food not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals that damage the good microbes in our guts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.ref: [원문 요약] 좋은 미생물을 기르는 방법: 요구르트·김치·낫또 등 유익한 박테리아가 든 음식 섭취, 마늘·양파·비가공 곡물 섭취, 가공식품 회피.

Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning. questions.stem:
다음 글의 요지로 볼 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문 요지] 유익한 미생물이 먼저 몸을 점유하여 해로운 세균을 막고, 면역 체계를 촉진하여 좋은 물질과 나쁜 물질을 구별한다 → 천연 방어막 역할.
det.correct:
✅ ② defense: 미생물이 해로운 세균의 성장을 '막고', 면역 체계를 '촉진'하여 질병으로부터 보호하는 '방어' 역할.
❌ ① replacement(대체물) — 미생물이 무언가를 대체하는 것이 아님
❌ ③ symptom(증상) — 미생물은 증상이 아닌 보호 역할
❌ ④ threat(위협) — 미생물이 위협이 아닌 방어 역할
det.tip: 💡 미생물의 역할: ① 선점(occupying) → 유해균 차단, ② 면역 촉진(facilitate) → 물질 구별. 즉 '천연 방어막(natural defense)' 역할.

questions.passage: Other microbes regulate the appetite hormone, which makes a person feel full or hungry. Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat. One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. Similarly, doing the reverse made the lean mouse gain weight.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The mouse experiment suggests that gut bacteria play a decisive role in determining an individual's __________.

Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.

❌ ③ 미생물 연구에 더 많은 예산을 투자해야 한다 — 예산/투자 언급 없음
